de 256 bits : impossible de revenir au t: of 256 bits: impossible to get back to the text, and changing a single letter changes the whole fingerprint (the avalanche effect). Websites keep the fingerprint of your password, not the password. So it is not encryption: there is no decryption.
est le chiffrement qu'utilisent les banq: is the encryption used by banks, Wi-Fi and HTTPS. Your password is turned into a 256-bit key (PBKDF2, 200,000 rounds, with a random salt), then the message is encrypted with a random vector: the same text gives a different result every time. GCM adds a signature: change a single character and decryption fails. The password is never saved.
